Context/Background:
Intraductal papillary neoplasms (IPNs),  including intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMNs), intraductal oncocytic papillary neoplasms (IOPNs), and intraductal tubulopapillary neoplasms (ITPNs), are clinically detectable macroscopic non-invasive cyst-forming lesions, some of which progress to invasive pancreatic cancer. Proteins and glycoproteins have proven to be useful clinical biomarkers for classifying cyst-forming neoplasms in the pancreas.Here, we used proteomics and glycoproteomics to characterize a series of histologically and genetically well-characterized surgically resected IPNs, including IPMNs and IOPNs.

Our analysis included 69 IPNs (64 IPMNs and 5 IOPNs), 76 macro-dissected grossly normal duct tissues (NDs, with 32 of the 76 NDs coming from the same resection specimens as the IPNs), and 32 cyst fluid samples (22 from matched IPMN patients, 3 matched IOPN patients, 2 from unrelated IPMN patients, and 5 other cysts).
Prompt: Look at the list of glycoproteins upregulated in IPMNS with both KRAS and GNAS mutations compared to wild-type IPMNs and explain the pattern with activities of signaling pathways.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
A site-specific N-glycoproteomics survey (Wang_2025_TableS3I) compared IPMNs harboring concurrent KRAS and GNAS mutations against wild-type IPMNs. Ninety upregulated glycoprotein sites (FDR < 0.05) were identified, including known O-glycosylation enzymes (GALNT3, GALNT5, C1GALT1C1, ST6GALNAC1, GCNT1) and receptor- and adhesion-type glycoproteins (ADAM10, MET, ERBB3, EPHA2, ITGA6). Tissue source: surgically resected IPMNs; contrast: KRAS+GNAS double mutants vs. wild-type IPMNs; assay: glycoproteomics (LC-MS/MS). Details on sample numbers, replicates, and histology: not specified.

Keywords  
KRAS mutation; GNAS mutation; O-glycosylation; PI3K-Akt signaling; receptor tyrosine kinases

Candidate Genes  
ADAM10; MET; ERBB3; EPHA2; ITGA6

Pathway Enrichments  
Up/Down ratios by GSEA (ranked by log₂FC)  
• KEGG_2016: 0 up, 0 down (no sig. terms)  
• GO_Biological_Process_2023: 0 up, 0 down (no sig. terms)  
• Reactome_Pathways_2024: 1 up (100%), 0 down (0%)  
• MSigDB_Hallmark_2020: 0 up, 0 down (no sig. terms)

Reactome_Pathways_2024 (UP):  
| Theme                                 | Direction | Leading Genes         |  
|---------------------------------------|-----------|-----------------------|  
| Post-translational Protein Modification | Up        | MUC5AC; GALNT3; GALNT5 |

KEGG_2016 (UP): none  
KEGG_2016 (DOWN): none  
GO_Biological_Process_2023 (UP): none  
GO_Biological_Process_2023 (DOWN): none  
MSigDB_Hallmark_2020 (UP): none  
MSigDB_Hallmark_2020 (DOWN): none

Analysis  
GSEA of ranked glycoproteins yielded a single Reactome signal for broad “Post-translational Protein Modification,” driven by mucin family members (MUC5AC) and glycosyltransferases (GALNT3, GALNT5). ORA on the FDR‐filtered, upregulated proteins highlighted a strong mucin-type O-glycan biosynthesis signature (5/36 genes, adj. p ≈ 4 × 10⁻⁶) plus enrichment of PI3K-Akt signaling (5/354 genes, adj. p ≈ 0.04) and KRAS pathway components. This dual pattern reflects how KRAS/GNAS mutations both upregulate glycosylation machinery (altering mucin and core O-glycan structures) and remodel receptor/adhesion glycoproteins (e.g., ADAM10, MET, ERBB3, EPHA2, ITGA6) to potentiate PI3K-Akt and downstream MAPK/ERK signaling.

Targeted (keyword-guided) subset  
Mucin-Type O-Glycans:  
| Term                                | Overlap | Adj. P-value   | Genes                                   |  
|-------------------------------------|---------|----------------|-----------------------------------------|  
| Mucin type O-glycan biosynthesis    | 5/36    | 3.96 × 10⁻⁶   | ST6GALNAC1; C1GALT1C1; GALNT5; GALNT3; GCNT1 |  
| Other types of O-glycan biosynthesis| 3/47    | 1.26 × 10⁻²   | C1GALT1C1; GALNT5; GALNT3               |

Signaling Pathways:  
| Term                                           | Adj. P-value | Genes                                  |  
|------------------------------------------------|-------------|----------------------------------------|  
| Epithelial cell signaling in H. pylori infection | 2.03 × 10⁻² | ATP6V0A2; ADAM10; MET                  |  
| PI3K-Akt signaling pathway                      | 4.08 × 10⁻² | ERBB3; ITGA6; MET; EPHA2; YWHAH        |  
| KRAS Signaling Up                               | 8.83 × 10⁻² | TSPAN13; GALNT3; TLR8                  |

Key Genes/Proteins (leading edge)  
Upregulated Glycosylation Enzymes and RTKs  
| Gene         | Direction | Role/Function                                       | Pathway(s)                          |  
|--------------|-----------|-----------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------|  
| ST6GALNAC1   | Up        | α2,6-sialyltransferase; terminal sialylation of O-glycans | O-glycan biosynthesis               |  
| C1GALT1C1    | Up        | Chaperone/core 1 β3Gal-transferase accessory         | O-glycan core 1 assembly            |  
| GALNT3       | Up        | Initiates mucin-type O-glycosylation                 | O-glycan initiation; KRAS Up (Hallmark) |  
| GALNT5       | Up        | Initiates mucin-type O-glycosylation                 | O-glycan initiation                 |  
| GCNT1        | Up        | Core 2 β1,6-N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase         | Core extension of O-glycans         |  
| ADAM10       | Up        | Metalloprotease; ectodomain shedding of RTK ligands | EGFR/MET axis; H. pylori epithelium signaling |  
| MET          | Up        | Hepatocyte growth factor RTK; PI3K-Akt, MAPK signaling | PI3K-Akt; cell scattering            |  
| ERBB3        | Up        | EGFR family RTK; PI3K-Akt adaptor                   | PI3K-Akt pathway                    |  
| EPHA2        | Up        | Ephrin receptor; cell adhesion, motility             | PI3K-Akt; axon guidance             |  
| ITGA6        | Up        | Integrin α6; adhesion to laminin                    | PI3K-Akt; cell–ECM interactions      |  

Downregulated Glycoproteins  
| Gene | Direction | Role/Function | Pathway(s) |  
|------|-----------|---------------|------------|  
| None | —         | —             | —          |

Comparisons  
No parallel data in wild-type vs. other IPN subtypes is available here; however, the glycosylation signature aligns with known mucin remodeling in KRAS-driven pancreatic lesions. RTK and integrin glycoprotein upregulation further underscores mutation-driven signaling potentiation.

Implications  
1. Enhanced O-glycan biosynthesis suggests that mucin-modifying enzymes could serve as biomarkers or targets to distinguish KRAS/GNAS mutant IPMNs.  
2. Upregulation of ADAM10 and RTKs (MET, ERBB3, EPHA2) indicates a feed-forward loop between glycan remodeling and growth-factor signaling in precursor lesions.  
3. Therapeutic strategies combining RTK inhibitors with glycosylation-modifying agents may blunt aberrant PI3K-Akt/MAPK signaling and impede progression to invasiveness.

Next Steps & Clarification  
1. Validate site-specific glycopeptide changes by lectin blotting or glycan-specific antibodies in additional IPMN cohorts.  
2. Test if pharmacologic inhibition of GALNT3/C1GALT1C1 alters RTK activation and downstream signaling in organoid or cell models.  
3. Assess the functional impact of ADAM10-mediated ectodomain shedding on HGF/MET and EGFR ligand availability in IPMN tissues.  
4. Clarify presence/absence of other thematic enrichments:  
   – Cell-cycle or mitotic processes: not observed (no significant GO terms)  
   – Stress-response pathways: not observed (no Hallmark stress signals)  
   – Metabolic pathways beyond glycosylation: limited (KRAS-Up and glycolysis border Hallmark but FDR > 0.05)
